newsitem.title: FRANCE: Rest of French troops to reach Albania on Friday.
newsitem.headline: Rest of French troops to reach Albania on Friday.

text.p: The French contingent in a multinational security force in Albania will reach full strength of about 1,000 men on Friday when more soldiers land in a northern port, the Defence Ministry said on Thursday.

The new group, of 600 men and 200 vehicles, would arrive by ship at the port of Durres. About 400 French soldiers and 100 vehicles landed earlier this week as part of the U.N.-approved mission to the anarchic Balkan state.
Two logistical support vessels would also arrive in Durres by April 21. The ministry said it expected the force to be fully deployed and operational by May 5. It has a three-month mandate.
The first troops in the Italian-led force arrived this week and are now guarding the main port of Durres and checking roads and bridges to ensure the safety of aid convoys.
The French force found relative calm on its arrival in Albania and the Defence Ministry said there was some evidence the country was starting to return to normal.

Some 300 people have been killed and 700 injured during the weeks of anarchy and banditry that swept Europe's poorest nation after fraudulent investment schemes wiped out the savings of many families.
"The start of the operation has gone well," said Pierre Servent, Defence Ministry spokesman. "It would seem that, here and there, we can observe a certain return to normality."
But Servent cautioned that it was still early days and that uncertainty remained. "All this must be taken with a great deal of caution. We are only at the beginning," he said.
The French air force has pre-positioned air attack elements in Italy in case they are needed and four medical evacuation helicopters are on standby in Brindisi.
